links.claim: MAX is the best-supported non-null candidate among the listed TFs because it is highly expressed in glioblastoma (58.6 TPM, rank 48/1626), has an ENCODE peak containing the variant in H1 (E08/E19), and c-Myc/MAX is literature-linked to hTERT promoter activation via Ets/E-box motifs (E21e/E21f). However, no glioblastoma ChIP peak at this site is provided, E04 says no ENCODE biosample matches the expression context, and no QBiC-SELEX/allele-specific data exist; the hypothesized direction that alt A binds MAX more strongly is a model prediction, not established.

VEP annotates ENSR5_C5GP enhancer at the variant (E01), but E03 reports that no ENCODE cCRE overlaps the variant and the nearest pELS is 75 bp away, so the element assignment is uncertain and the variant may sit adjacent to, rather than inside, the active element.

TERT is only 0.5 kb from the TSS (E02), and MAX/Myc literature supports hTERT promoter activation (E21e/E21f), but there is no Hi-C/3C, reporter, or perturbation evidence in this case linking this specific upstream site to TERT.
Glioblastoma is the supplied expression context and MAX is expressed there (E08), but there is no glioblastoma ChIP at this site (E04) and no TERT expression data in glioblastoma are supplied.

TERT is repeatedly implicated in glioblastoma/melanoma/bladder cancer in the literature (E18), but the genetic support here is weak: E16 is a hypertension credible set with PIP 0.00, and E20 shows TERT is not commonly essential in CNS lines (median -0.00, 2% dependent).

predictions: MAX occupies chr5:1295601 in glioblastoma cells, with stronger binding to the A allele than the G allele.

falsified_if: MAX does not occupy the variant site in glioblastoma cells, or the G/A change has no effect on MAX binding or TERT regulation.

We chose the hepatoblastoma cell line Hep-G2 and the lung cancer cell line A-549 for this proof-of-principle study, as they contained two different kinds of variants, namely the activating mutation C228T in the TERT core promoter and the common SNP rs[masked] in the THOR region, respectively.
These variants were targeted in an allele-specific manner using sgRNA-guided dCas9-DNMT3A-3L complexes.
They generate de novo binding sites for E-twenty-six (ETS) transcription factors causing increased TERT transcription.
The luciferase reporter assay was used to functionally characterize the identified alterations.

Using chromatinized bacterial artificial chromosome (BAC) reporters in human fibroblasts, we found that ETV5 and c-Myc/MYC-associated factor X (MAX) synergistically activate the hTERT promoter via two identical, but inverted, composite Ets/E-box motifs enclosing the core promoter.
Mutations of Ets or E-box sites in either DNA motif abolished the activation and reduced or eliminated the synergism.
Newly described non-coding mutations in the Tert promoter region of many cancer cells (19 %) in two key positions, C250T and C228T, have added another layer of complexity to telomerase reactivation.
These mutations create novel consensus sequences for transcription factors which can enhance Tert expression.
